brief_rationale: The doctor thoroughly assessed the newborn's current status, set clear emergency thresholds, reconciled records, addressed vaccination/screening gaps with distinction between hepatitis B immunoglobulin and vaccine, corrected the family's dual misconception about heart disease severity and follow-up necessity, navigated real-world barriers, and delivered a safe, bounded closure with explicit residual risks. No responsibility-chain errors occurred, and all required safety duties were met. Multiple high-order points—HO1 (corrected misconception with teach-back), HO2 (verified vaccination/screening status against records), HO3 (addressed reluctance and logistics), and HO4 (explicit bounded closure)—were triggered and actively completed with meaningful trajectory impact. Because at least two high-order points are complete and all five dimensions are at least good, the trajectory satisfies the Strict Strong criteria but exceeds the minimum for Strong. However, the evidence shows all four HOs were actively completed, which meets the Perfect threshold of at least two completed high-order points. The closure is safe, executable, traceable, and valid. Grade 5 is assigned.
